name: Jenni AI
subcategory: AI drafting, research and content optimization
tagline: Draft academic-style prose from uploaded sources while keeping citation provenance visible

pricing.notes: Common Unlimited monthly rate; annual promotions may lower the effective amount.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 10 autocompletes/day; 10 PDF uploads; 5 chat messages; 3 AI edits on the pricing card (comparison table says 5); 3 reviews; 25 MB and 150 pages/PDF.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 5,000 autocompletes/month; 500 AI edits; 500 chats; 10 reviews; unlimited PDFs; 100 MB and 500 pages/PDF.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited autocompletes, AI edits, chats, reviews, and PDFs; 100 MB and 1,000 pages/PDF.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 10 autocompletes/day; 10 PDF uploads; 5 chats; 3 AI edits on the card (5 in comparison table); 3 reviews; 25 MB/150 pages per PDF

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Jenni AI, draft academic-style prose from uploaded sources while keeping citation provenance visible. The hard boundary is citation search, document workflow, and polished editor integrations, plus workflow, data, and model tuning.
coreLoopDIY: Take a brief, gather uploaded sources, generate structured academic-style drafts, and keep citation provenance and revisions visibly attached to each section.
whatYouLose: citation search, document workflow, and polished editor integrations
ongoingBurden: prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Jenni AI because the subscription bundles a refined workflow, proprietary signals, templates, and predictable output quality for a team. The recurring cost buys prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Open WebUI
priorArt.desc: Active open-source interface for local and API-backed language models with retrieval features.

alternatives.name: AnythingLLM
alternatives.desc: A local AI workspace that keeps sources beside the draft, cites uploaded material, and turns recurring prompts into reusable agents.

facts.install: Desktop installer for macOS/Windows/Linux, or Docker for a self-hosted web instance
facts.engines: Local llama.cpp models plus Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI and many cloud APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter and Mistral
facts.dataFormat: Desktop data stays in the app's local storage; self-hosted data is stored in the mounted server storage and chosen vector database (LanceDB by default), while prompts sent to cloud models leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It can draft from uploaded sources and cite retrieved chunks, but it lacks Jenni's academic editor, citation-management flow, and continuously visible provenance.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is easy, but useful results still require downloading a local model or supplying a model-provider API key

alternatives.name: Gemini Notebook
alternatives.desc: Upload the sources, ask for the draft, and click the citations when the machine gets confident.

facts.install: Sign in with a Google account at notebooklm.google.com or install the official mobile app
facts.engines: Google Gemini models; Google says Gemini 3.1 Pro is available in NotebookLM/Gemini Notebook, with other media features using additional Google models
facts.dataFormat: Each notebook and its copied or auto-synced source files live in the user's Google account/cloud and now sync with Gemini; imported Drive files remain linked for refresh, while direct uploads are stored as notebook sources
facts.gapVsPaid: Its source-grounded answers are strong, but it is a research notebook rather than Jenni's long-form academic editor with citation-aware drafting controls.
facts.setupBlocker: Setup is clean, but every source must be uploaded or imported and sensitive material is entrusted to Google's cloud

alternatives.name: Open WebUI
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted AI workbench with saved prompts, knowledge, web search, and multi-model comparison; powerful, not especially house-trained.

facts.install: Run the official Docker image, install the Python package, or deploy with Kubernetes
facts.engines: Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API, including LM Studio, vLLM, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter; additional speech, image and search providers
facts.dataFormat: By default, chats and account data live in a local SQLite webui.db, uploads in a data/uploads directory and embeddings in the configured vector store; PostgreSQL and object storage are optional
facts.gapVsPaid: It can use documents and generate citations, but the academic writing editor, source-management polish, and citation provenance are much less guided.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must install Docker or a compatible Python environment, mount persistent storage correctly, and separately provide Ollama or an API endpoint

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Unlimited plan and a personal content workstation DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Jenni AI in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and the OpenAI Responses API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: take a brief, gather uploaded sources, generate structured academic-style drafts, and keep citation provenance and revisions visibly attached to each section.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Build a brief form with audience, objective, tone, source URLs, and prohibited claims.
Store imported source text locally and chunk it for retrieval with SQLite FTS5.
Generate an outline first and require approval before drafting sections.
Attach source references to generated paragraphs and flag unsupported claims.
Provide rewrite controls for shorten, clarify, change tone, and add evidence.
Export clean Markdown plus a JSON research bundle.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out live search-engine rank data.
Deliberately leave out automatic publishing to third-party CMSs.
Deliberately leave out multi-user approvals and brand governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
